evidence.text: The article identifies the mid-Western Zhou 豦簋 inscription as the earliest securely identifiable 干 in its account. It describes that form as a round shield-like body with a forked top; later Western Zhou forms replace the upper round feature with a short horizontal stroke, continued in later scripts. The attribution of proposed earlier Shang signs to 干 remains debated.
evidence.title: 商周時期的防護裝具與兵器：甲、冑、干、盾（四）

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.field: formation, early uses, competing analysis, and Shuowen
evidence.text: The database interprets oracle-bone and bronze 干 as a decorated shield. It cites an oracle-bone defensive use (合集 28059, 弜令戍干衛), bronze 豦簋 干戈 for the shield sense, and 毛公鼎 干吾王身 for a defensive use. It also reports Xu Zhongshu’s alternative that some oracle-bone 干 and 單 forms are variants depicting a forked hunting implement. Its quotation of Shuowen, 犯也。从反入，从一, is a Han-period explanation, not independent confirmation of the shield pictograph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — oraclePiece 干

evidence.field: 乾 structure, readings, and variant history
evidence.text: The dictionary quotes Shuowen’s analysis of 乾 as 从乙 with 倝聲. It records modern Mandarin gān and qián, and documents variant spellings from sources including the Tang 李晟碑 and a Wei tomb inscription. The entry supports 倝 as the traditional sound element in 乾, but does not establish 倝’s original depicted referent.
evidence.title: A00044 乾 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: This exact character entry gives Mandarin readings gān and qián. Local Unihan kMandarin rows supplied for this research also read 乾 qián gān; these are current readings, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup for U+4E7E (lookup attempted; page unavailable)

evidence.field: 幹 formation, sound role, readings, and senses
evidence.text: The dictionary says 幹 is not recorded in Shuowen and describes it as a vulgar form of 榦, with 倝 as sound element. It records Mandarin gàn and hán, and senses including structural timber, a body’s main part, principal, ability, affairs, and manage. It does not assign 干 “shield” a sound or semantic role inside 幹.
evidence.title: A01196 幹 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The entry gives Mandarin gàn (and hán for a separate reading). The exact supplied local Unihan kMandarin row for 幹 is gàn. The official character-specific Unihan URL was attempted but unavailable in this session; neither the local row nor this modern reading proves a historical sound role for 干 in 幹.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup for U+5E79 (lookup attempted; page unavailable)

evidence.field: 乾 dry reading and variant evidence
evidence.text: The dictionary distinguishes 乾 readings gān and qián and records gān-only variant spellings, including 亁, described as a vulgar spelling for the dry sense. It does not establish when the dry reading began or a semantic transition from 干 “shield.” The supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows distinguish dry 乾 MC kan, OC *[k]ˤar from heaven 乾 MC gjen, OC *[g](r)ar; these readings are local dataset checks, not external-page evidence.
evidence.title: A00044 乾 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The exact file 干-seal.svg is described as a vector of 干 in Shuowen seal-script style, sourced for its image to hanziyuan.net image s01611 and other character databases. The page lists a public-domain dedication for the vector representation, with attribution appreciated but not required. This is a modern redraw, not a dated artifact or proof of the shield interpretation. The alternate exact file Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg could not be opened, so its identity, pixels, and rights were not verified.

evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv exact rows; local row checked, official character page unavailable
evidence.text: Exact supplied Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows: 干 shield MC kan, OC *kˤa[r]; 干 pole MC kan, OC *[k]ˤar; 乾 dry MC kan, OC *[k]ˤar; 乾 heaven MC gjen, OC *[g](r)ar; 幹 stem/framework MC kanH, OC *[k]ˤar-s. The system distinguishes Middle Chinese and Old Chinese columns. These local readings alone do not show a graphic or phonetic relationship. No 倝 row was supplied in the local table, so its exact reading was not independently cross-checked there.

search_audit.outcome: Search results included the NTU CASE paleographic article, CUHK character entry, and Kotobank. Opened and inspected the CASE and CUHK pages; they report mid-Western Zhou secure evidence and competing shield versus hunting-implement interpretations.

search_audit.query: 乾 倝 聲 說文 乾 暵其乾矣 教育部 異體字字典
search_audit.outcome: Opened the official Ministry dictionary entry for 乾 and inspected the Shuowen sound-element account and recorded readings. The accessible entry supports 倝 as phonetic but does not identify its original referent.

search_audit.query: 幹 榦 倝 聲 教育部 異體字字典 幹 古案切
search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the Ministry dictionary entry: it describes 幹 as a vulgar form of 榦, with 倝 sound, and records gàn and hán readings and historical senses.

Opened the exact 干-seal.svg Commons page and inspected its description, image source attribution, and public-domain terms. The exact Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg page returned an internal error; its pixels, identity, and licensing remain unchecked.

gaps: No component-level phonetic relationship applies to 干 itself; it is interpreted as a whole-graph pictograph. The pictured implement’s ancient name and pronunciation are not independently recovered, but the shield interpretation does not depend on a whole-graph phonetic-loan claim.

The attribution of some proposed Shang signs to 干 remains disputed. No artifact glyph image was visually inspected in this research; descriptions of the script forms rely on the cited paleographic article and dictionary.

乾’s dry use and qián/heaven use have distinct recorded readings, but their semantic relationship and precise chronology are not established here. The prior packet’s claim of a Book of Odes dry attestation was not independently reopened in this pass.

幹 is described by the Ministry dictionary as a vulgar form of 榦 with 倝 as sound. This does not establish any phonetic or semantic role for 干 in 幹, nor does simplification chronology show derivation from the shield graph.

Modern reading data: local supplied Unihan rows are 干 gàn, 乾 qián gān, 幹 gàn. Character-specific official Unihan lookups for U+5E72, U+4E7E, and U+5E79 were attempted but did not return accessible pages. The Ministry dictionary independently verifies the relevant modern readings for 乾 and 幹; a separate inspected external source for Mandarin 干 was not obtained in this pass.

No 倝 row was supplied in the local Baxter–Sagart table; its pronunciation and original referent remain unverified here. The Ministry dictionary’s sound-element attribution is a source assertion, not a reconstruction or independent comparison.

The exact Commons seal vector’s metadata and declared identity were inspected, but the file pixels were not visually inspected; it is a modern seal-style redraw and should not be presented as an ancient artifact form.
The alternate Commons file Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg failed to open. No conclusions about its image identity, source, or reuse terms can be made.
